clue.text: Good time blondes have?

parts.note: blondes are fair-haired, so the jolly time they enjoy is playfully the amusement belonging to the fair ones; the phrase also means a fairground's merriment

explanation.surface: A question about whether blondes really have more fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on 'fair' meaning blonde: the fun that belongs to the fair-haired is also a fairground outing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the jollity of a travelling fairground, a classic good time.

clue.text: The dunce with the corpulent master

parts.note: corpulent means fat
a head is the master of a school, a headmaster

explanation.surface: A dim pupil and a stout schoolmaster stand side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAD is the British name for a headteacher, here 'master'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a stupid person, informally called a thickhead or idiot.

clue.text: You may hang on to it

definitions.text: You may hang on to it

parts.words: You may hang on to it
parts.note: reads like advice about clinging to something, but means a picture or coat is hung on this small metal spike

explanation.surface: Advice to keep hold of something precious.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is hung on a small metal pin hammered into the wall.

clue.text: Shuts up when the fellow's holding a gun

indicators.note: the fellow's letters hold the gun between them, one on each side

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, and the possessive 's gives S
a Sten is a British submachine gun, so 'a gun' gives A STEN

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent once a man produces a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten gun is the crossword's favourite firearm; F and the 's of 'fellow's' wrap A STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut up a house or box is to secure or close it fast.

clue.text: She-man!

parts.note: looks like an insult for an effeminate man, but means the man who wrote the novel She

explanation.surface: A jeering cry at a man thought unmanly.
explanation.walkthrough: She (1887) is the famous adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard; the word also means gaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of the novel She is the Victorian writer whose surname this is.

clue.text: What nobody can deny having achieved

definitions.text: What nobody can deny having achieved

parts.words: What nobody can deny having achieved
parts.note: reads as something undeniable, but a nobody (an obscure person) can truthfully deny having won renown

explanation.surface: A remark about an accomplishment beyond dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nobody' is a noun here: an unknown person, who has not won celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown or celebrity is exactly what an obscure nobody lacks.

clue.text: Keep away from the others, I note, at tea-break

parts.note: sol (soh) is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a break of the word tea shakes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reminds themselves to keep to themselves during the tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-break' hides the anagram: 'break' rearranges TEA to ATE, which follows I and SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart or quarantine from everyone else.

clue.text: Examination certificate

parts.note: sounds like a school exam diploma, but is a police document authorising the examination of premises

explanation.surface: A diploma received after passing a school test.
explanation.definitionFit: Police need a court-issued document before they may examine a property.

clue.text: Share the same bus-stop and are friends

definitions.meaning: boarding a bus at the same stop, taken literally
to be on good terms

explanation.surface: Commuters at one bus stop become pals.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally boarding together at a stop, and idiomatically being on friendly terms.

clue.text: Involves mending the net before one sets sail

indicators.note: the net's letters come before the sail's in the answer
mending the net reworks its three letters into a fresh order
the word sail is set into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting ready for sea means fixing the net before one hoists sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mending' turns NET into ENT and 'sets' turns SAIL into AILS; 'one' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: If a plan entails something, it necessarily includes or requires it.

clue.text: Yellow marsh animals are all about

indicators.note: the animals' word surrounds the marsh's word on every side

parts.note: game is wild animals hunted for sport
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: Creatures of the wetland swarm everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: GAMBOGE is a gum resin used as a yellow pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment from a Southeast Asian tree resin.

clue.text: It's used in casting the film

definitions.meaning: the winding spool of an angler's rod, used when casting a line
a spool of cinema film

explanation.surface: A tool used in choosing actors for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' suggests choosing actors, but it is fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing spool and a roll of cinema film share the name.

clue.text: A gong for dinner when the day is through

indicators.note: the day passes through the middle of the dinner word

parts.note: dinner is a meal
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A dinner gong sounding once the day's work is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for a decoration awarded for service.

clue.text: The pudding will be the starter, we're told

indicators.note: signals that the sound of the words matters, not their spelling

parts.note: a race starter's job is to say 'go'

explanation.surface: Diners learn the pudding will be served as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'starter' as a first course; it is the person who starts a race by saying 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy palm product made into a milk dessert.

clue.text: Makes work for civil servants

definitions.meaning: shapes or creates
official documents to be filled in, the stuff of bureaucracy

explanation.surface: A jibe that bureaucracy generates paperwork for officials.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape something is to create it; officials process printed documents to be completed.

clue.text: Nothing on the girl to catch

indicators.note: in a down entry the nothing goes on (below) the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A girl wearing nothing is easy to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: LASS is northern British and Scottish for girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope is used to capture cattle; as a verb it means to snare.

clue.text: Cover up the hole ourselves. It's an eyesore

parts.note: to hide is to cover up
O looks like a hole
us means ourselves

explanation.surface: Someone urges filling in an unsightly hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely ugly, like an eyesore, is repulsive to look at.

clue.text: Caught in a maze of detail, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the caught letter sits inside the jumbled detail
a maze twists the letters of detail into a tangled new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone lost in fussy details, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a maze of' jumbles DETAIL into DIALET, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of a language is a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Try a couple of times to get a new temp

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them make TT

indicators.note: a new version of temp has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An office tries twice to hire a fresh temporary worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TEMP into EMPT, which ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try or effort.

clue.text: On the journey back, I see, from the capital

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: the I and the see are read backwards as a pair

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A traveller on the way home from a city glimpses something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I + LO into OLI, after TRIP. Tripoli is the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Goes at the time I'm leaving port

parts.note: goes means tries, as in has a go

indicators.note: I'm leaving means those letters depart from the time word

parts.note: time taken as itself
I'm taken as the letters I and M

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a departure from a harbour at the scheduled hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' strips IM from TIME, leaving TE after TRIES. Trieste is an Adriatic port in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a seaport on the Adriatic in northeast Italy.

clue.text: Handing over, but it's only temporary

definitions.meaning: giving something to someone, as with a ball
fleeting or transient

explanation.surface: A hand-over that is described as merely temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing a ball is handing it on; a passing fancy is a fleeting one.

clue.text: Irritable as a bird gets when a little hungry?

definitions.meaning: touchy or grumpy, a sense of the word in American use
slightly wanting food, as a bird might be ready to peck

explanation.surface: A bird gets cranky when it wants a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a bird gets' plays on pecking, linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mildly hungry in Britain and, in American usage, testy.

clue.text: In semi-panic, the fool turns into a dead-end

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'In semi-panic, the fool turns into a dead-end': IMP + ASS + E or similar cannot be built from 'semi-panic' as held; likely an OCR garble, and no source gives the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: In semi-panic, the fool turns into a dead-end

clue.text: A bird-grouse

definitions.meaning: a wading marshbird such as the water bird of that name
to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: A game bird is named as a grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail is a marsh bird; to rail against something is to complain.

clue.text: Because it makes a nice change on Sunday

indicators.note: the changed nice is put on next to the Sunday letter
a change of nice alters its letter order

explanation.surface: A Sunday is pleasant because it brings a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NICE into INCE, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction, the word means for the reason that.

clue.text: Not much of a place

definitions.meaning: a small amount
a location

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a small town.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quantity is a spot of something, and a location is a spot.

clue.text: Rolled home

definitions.meaning: pressed level with a roller, as a lawn or pastry
an apartment, the British word for a dwelling of one floor

explanation.surface: A rolled-up item kept in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a flat is an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolled pastry is pressed level; a British apartment is a home.

clue.text: It stunts a tot's growth!

parts.note: sounds like something that keeps a child small, but a tot is a measure of spirits, and saying this word stops the pourer from adding more

explanation.surface: A warning about something that keeps toddlers small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say when' is said by someone pouring a drink; the guest answers with this word to stop the tot getting bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: The guest's cue word stops a host from pouring a larger measure.

clue.text: They may be in soup mugs

definitions.meaning: pasta strands floating in a broth
fools, gullible people

explanation.surface: Something served in soup cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' looks like cups, but means simpletons.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta strands go into broth, and the word is also slang for silly people.

clue.text: Quickly demolishing most of the shanties

indicators.note: knocking down the shacks breaks their letters up into a new order
most of the word loses one of its letters

parts.note: shanties taken as written

explanation.surface: Shacks are swiftly torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops one S from SHANTIES, and 'demolishing' rearranges the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To act hurriedly is to act fast.

clue.text: Much the same as before-a few pence

definitions.meaning: hardly any difference from the previous state
a small amount of coins

explanation.surface: Things are unchanged, says someone counting coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly any difference from before, and also a handful of coins.
